qs.q: Which laboratory finding is characteristic of a patient with hyperglycemia caused by an insulinoma rather than exogenous insulin administration?
o: C. Low insulin and high C-peptide
B. High insulin and low C-peptide
D. Low insulin and low C-peptide
A. High insulin and high C-peptide
qs.e: Insulin is secreted with equimolar amounts of C-peptide, meaning endogenous hyperinsulinism from an insulinoma results in high levels of both. Exogenous insulin administration leads to high insulin but low C-peptide levels.

qs.q: Whipple's triad for insulinoma consists of
o: Hypercalcaemia, renal stones, and peptic ulcer disease.
Hypoglycaemic symptoms, documented low glucose level, and symptom relief after glucose intake.
Diarrhoea, flushing, and right‑sided valvular heart disease.
Hypertension, headache, and palpitations occurring together.
qs.e: Most common pancreatic NET, 90% benign. Suppressed C-peptide during hypoglycaemia if exogenous insulin; elevated C-peptide in insulinoma.
